Meeting Header:
Date: 2026-09-24
Start time: 16:00 UTC
Duration: 48 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Samir Patel (Redwood SE), Lena Torres (Azura CTO), Devon Park (Azura ML), Nina Brooks (Azura Security)

transcript_full:
[00:00] Maya Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, I'm Maya with Redwood, this is Samir on the SE side. quick intro?
[00:12] Lena Torres: Hi, Lena here, CTO at Azura Labs. We're exploring infra for our customer-facing question-answering features. Main concerns are latency and PII handling.
[00:25] Samir Patel: great, thanks. quick context questions — are you planning to start on hosted/self-serve or do you expect a dedicated footprint from day one?
[00:38] Devon Park: Ideally self-serve to kick off, we want to try the API, validate quality, then move to Dedicated if we need predictable throughput.
[00:48] Nina Brooks: Security note — we'll need SOC 2 and KMS integration if we go beyond POC. Also curious about VPC or on-prem options.
[01:02] Maya Chen: totally understood. For PLG quickstart, we have free credits and a self-serve signup flow, many teams get to first token in under 10 minutes, often 5–15 minutes depending on oauth/key rotation and network. Samir — want to add specifics?
[01:18] Samir Patel: yeah, so typical path: sign up, create API key in console, run quickstart script — we provide SDKs (python/node) and a sample app. If you follow the guide and your firewall allows outbound, first token is usually minute range; if you want to run streaming responses or function calling, that's also supported out-of-the-box.
[01:38] Devon Park: nice. about cost — any rough numbers for small chat workloads? we're looking at 20–230k queries/month.
[01:45] Maya Chen: for hosted PLG, pricing is usage-based per token and per-embedding. we can send example pricing bands; for 20–230k queries it depends on model choice and prompt length. we also have Redwood Optimize recommendations — batching and KV cache can lower unit costs.
[02:02] Lena Torres: and Dedicated — when do teams move to that? is it an enterprise process?
[02:09] Samir Patel: teams typically start hosted, then move to Dedicated once they need guaranteed throughput or data isolation. Dedicated has reserved GPU pools, autoscaling policies, SLA backed latency targets; it is contract-based but we try to make the transition smooth.
[02:24] Nina Brooks: about Private/VPC — can we manage keys in our KMS? HSM?
[02:29] Maya Chen: yes, Redwood Private supports customer-managed KMS integration and on-prem packages. for VPC deployments we provide a control-plane that can sit in your network, and you can bring your own HSM for key management. we'll share the architecture doc.
[02:45] Devon Park: performance — what's typical P95 for generation? we care under 150ms P95 for short prompts.
[02:52] Samir Patel: depends on model and sequence length. we optimize kernel selection and batching; for smaller seq lengths and quantized models we often see single-digit token latencies but end-to-end P95 in the 100–200ms ballpark on dedicated hardware. for hosted, network adds some variability. we can run micro-benchmarks during the pilot.
[03:15] Lena Torres: are there any gotchas with the quickstart? our infra team is paranoid about open egress.
[03:21] Maya Chen: gotchas — corporate firewall blocking outbound, strict proxy rules, or blocked websockets for streaming. our quickstart has fallback polling if websockets blocked, but SE help is sometimes needed. also rate limits and quotas early on — we'll show how to request increases.
[03:39] Devon Park: we'd want a baseline benchmark: 1) run 1k sample queries, measure latency and token cost, 2) try small caching, 3) evaluate model variants. can Redwood run that or we run?
[03:51] Samir Patel: we typically provide a benchmark template and can run jointly. Samir: we'll send the spreadsheet and a script.
[04:02] Nina Brooks: security — we need SOC 2, ISO and an updated security questionnaire; also retention and deletion policies for logs and prompts.
[04:11] Maya Chen: we have a SOC 2 report and can share it under NDA; we support configurable retention and audit logs in Redwood Console. for sensitive PII we recommend Private or Dedicated with customer-managed KMS.
[04:24] Lena Torres: timeline — we're hoping to evaluate in the next 3–4 weeks, decide by mid-October.
[04:31] Maya Chen: sounds good; for PLG quickstart we can get the team onboarded this week, free credits applied, and a first benchmark in 1–2 weeks.
[04:40] Devon Park: any friction on credentials? rotating keys?
[04:43] Samir Patel: we support key rotation in console and recommend short-lived keys for production with our token exchange flow.
[04:50] Maya Chen: recap — we'll send quickstart link, sample app, free credits details, benchmark spreadsheet, and SOC2/security docs. Samir will set up the deep dive and benchmark session with Devon.
[04:59] Lena Torres: sounds good. one more — competitor question: we tested OpenAI and Replicate, what are major differences?
[05:07] Samir Patel: can speak high level — Oak: OpenAI has broad model catalog and ecosystem; Redwood focuses on production inference economics and unified serving across hosted/dedicated/private plus observability and rollback controls. Replicate is more model-distribution focused. we'll add a short comparison in the follow-up.
[05:28] Maya Chen: ok, next steps and deadlines, and we'll send calendar invites. thanks everyone.
[05:36] (meeting ends)
